text: In Levin's account of development and regeneration, the property of reaching the same correct final anatomical state from different starting conditions and by different routes — the cybernetic hallmark of genuine goal-directedness, explained by attractor dynamics — is called ___.
explanation: Equifinality is reaching the same endpoint from varied initial states, as when planaria regenerate correct anatomy from many different fragments. A fixed mechanical program cannot do this (changing the start changes the outcome), so equifinality is treated as the signature of goal-directedness, produced by a stable attractor drawing the system toward the target state.
